Work ONLY in the git worktree /home/ubuntu/english-only (detached at origin/main, deps installed). Never touch other directories. Read /home/ubuntu/english-only/AGENTS.md first: it has strict rules (no code comments allowed, no `as` assertions outside tests, explicit .ts import extensions, all UI text from catalogs, a pre-commit fence). Do NOT commit, push, or use git write commands; leave changes uncommitted for me to review.

GOAL: SurveyBeat ships English only for now. The owner said "get rid of German for now and focus only on English". German must be removable and later re-addable by adding a literal and catalogs, so KEEP the locale plumbing (the `Locale` type, `messagesFor(locale)`, `Record<Locale, ...>` tables, API fields `locale`/`detectedLocale`/`defaultLocale`, DB columns) but shrink it to one locale.

DO:
1. `packages/domain/src/people/Locale.ts`: `Locale = Schema.Literals(["en"])`. Keep matchLocale/browserLocale/resolveLocale working (they then only ever return "en" or undefined).
2. Delete German catalogs and pages: apps/web/src/messages/de.ts, apps/web/src/messages/answer.de.ts, apps/web/src/answer/de.ts, packages/emails/src/messages/de.ts, apps/web/de/answer.html. Remove every use: the `tables` maps in apps/web/src/messages/locale.ts and packages/emails/src/messages/index.ts, apps/web/vite.config.ts (answer-de entry, "de/answer.html" handling, answerDe import), apps/web/vite.site.config.ts and apps/web/src/site/render.ts (the /de landing page, the footer language link / `site.footer.language` key if it only served German), the German branch of the weekly team health Template in packages/domain/src/pulses/Template.ts (keep the English one; keep `weeklyTeamHealth(locale)` signature), and any /de route or de-specific link logic in packages/emails/src/links.ts, packages/cloudflare/src/ServerPages.ts, PageRoutes.ts.
3. Remove the language picker UI: the per-Person Language field (apps/web/src/app/directory.ts `LanguageChoice`, `languageField`, account menu) and the Settings "Default language" section, with their Foldkit messages/update branches/handlers in apps/web/src/app/App.ts, api.ts, session.ts etc., and the catalog keys `language.*`, `settings.defaultLanguage*`. Keep the English UI otherwise identical. Keep the API schema fields in packages/api optional/compatible so nothing else breaks; just stop sending a language from the UI. (If removing a field from an HttpApi payload is cleaner and nothing else needs it, tell me what you did.)
4. IMPORTANT data safety: production rows may already hold 'de' in D1/DO columns `person.locale`, `person.detected_locale`, `organization.default_locale` (CHECK allows 'de'; do NOT add a migration that rewrites them). In packages/cloudflare/src/SqlDirectory.ts the row schemas currently use `Locale` and would FAIL to decode a stored 'de'. Make reads lenient: decode those columns as strings (nullable) and map anything that isn't a known Locale to null (person) or DEFAULT_LOCALE (organization). Add a test in SqlDirectory.test.ts that a row holding 'de' reads back as null/"en" instead of failing. Check any other place that decodes stored locales (grep `Locale` in packages/cloudflare/src, e.g. emailLocaleOf, email send storage in domain/email) for the same risk and apply the same leniency.
5. Docs: add `docs/adr/0025-english-only-for-now.md` (short, same style as docs/adr/0018-german-localization.md: title, 1 intro line, bullets, Consequences). It supersedes the Release 2 German rollout of ADR 0018 (do not delete 0018; add a line at the top of 0018 saying it is superseded by 0025 for now). Content: English is the only shipped language; locale plumbing, typed-catalog approach, and Redaction's German phone-number cases stay; stored 'de' values read back as unset; to bring German back add the literal, a catalog per surface, the bilingual Template, and an answer page per locale. Update SPEC.md line ~135 ("Interface languages at launch are English and German") and the German translation mention near line 252 to say English only for now (see ADR 0025). Update docs/infra.md or AGENTS.md only if they mention German pages.
6. Tests: update or delete tests that assert German behavior (locale.test.ts, messages.test.ts, budget.test.ts, round-context.test.ts, render.test.ts + snapshot, Template.test.ts, ServerPages.test.ts, DirectoryApi.test.ts, App.story/scene tests, etc.). Do not weaken coverage of English behavior; keep the remaining locale tests meaningful (e.g. unknown tags like "de-DE" now resolve to undefined/"en" default). Keep Redaction German phone cases untouched.

VALIDATE (run from /home/ubuntu/english-only, in this order, fix until all pass): `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check` (run `pnpm format` to fix), `pnpm check:ledger`, `pnpm check:comments`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:privacy`, `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build`. Do not add lint disables or Effect diagnostic overrides (the ledger only shrinks; deleting some is welcome). Do not run the adapter tests that deploy to workerd unless a typecheck says you must.

REPORT: list of files deleted/changed, anything you chose differently from this brief and why, and the exact outputs (pass/fail counts) of each validation command.

1	# SurveyBeat
2	
3	Cloudflare-only Effect app. One Durable Object per Organization is the system of record; D1 holds only the global index and auth/email bookkeeping, never survey content. Three Workers serve the app/API (`MainWorker`), the answer page's submission path (`SubmissionWorker`), and the static landing page (`SiteWorker`, ADR 0020).
4	
5	Read `SPEC.md` (authoritative spec), `GLOSSARY.md` (domain vocabulary), and `docs/adr/` (binding decisions) before changing behavior. `docs/infra.md` covers stages, Better Auth sign-in, email, and observability. For Effect, Alchemy, Foldkit, XState, a new lint rule, or a Cloudflare resource, start at the [ratstack agent guide](https://ratstack.sh/llms.txt) and follow the Ratstack section.
6	
7	## Ground rules
8	
9	- Use glossary terms exactly: Pulse (not Survey), Person (not User), Round (not instance), Submission (not Response). Do not drift to the "avoid" synonyms.
10	- If a change contradicts an ADR, say so and add a new ADR under `docs/adr/`; never silently override one.
11	- Issues and specs live in GitHub issues (`gh`); conventions are in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`. Commit subjects name the release slice, e.g. `R1 03: ...`.
12	- Privacy invariants are release blockers (SPEC §7): anonymous Submissions store no Person and no time (ADR 0005), comments are redacted at store time (ADR 0009), and every shown aggregate obeys the minimum group size (ADR 0004).
13	
14	## Ratstack
15	
16	SurveyBeat keeps its own packages, commands, and deploy steps in this file. The [ratstack agent guide](https://ratstack.sh/llms.txt) is the reference for Effect, Alchemy, Foldkit, and XState. The template's package list and deploy steps describe the reference repo at [joelhooks/rat-stack](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack).
17	
18	When the installed `effect` package contains `AGENTS.md`, read that file first. It matches the pin. Then search the guide before you change Effect, Alchemy, Foldkit, XState, a lint rule, or a Cloudflare resource. Read the page the search returns, including the rule or skill that owns the change.
19	
20	Use `search`, then `read`. One program can do both through `POST https://ratstack.sh/api/execute`, as `tools.search({ query, limit })` and `tools.read({ id })`. That program cannot import, export, or call `fetch`. An MCP client uses the same tools at `https://ratstack.sh/mcp`.
21	
22	This repo has the floor from that guide. Strict TypeScript, oxlint, `oxfmt --check`, Vitest with `@effect/vitest`, and the fence below are in place. `oxlint.config.ts` extends Ultracite core and loads the Foldkit, anti-slop, effect-tests and pattern plugins; `docs/agents/lint-scope.md` lists what runs at `error` and every rule that is off while the restyle in #216 is outstanding. Alchemy and Foldkit are in use. ADR 0008 and ADR 0011 record that choice. Add another template package only when an ADR names it.
23	
24	The fence is `.githooks/` and `scripts/fence/`. `pnpm install` sets `core.hooksPath` to `.githooks`. The pre-commit hook runs `pnpm check` and then `pnpm test`, and refuses the commit when a step fails. Fix the failure and commit again so the hook runs. Claude Code denies a `git` command that passes `--no-verify` or sets `core.hooksPath`, through `scripts/fence/vcs-command-policy.mjs`. The post-commit hook reports a commit that skipped the gate. CI also runs the privacy suite and the web build. The hook stops after `pnpm test`.
25	
26	Put a reason in a name, a type, a test, a commit message, or an ADR. `pnpm lint` enforces it: `no-comments/no-comments` and `no-comments/directive-reason` run at `error` (test files and `infra/tests` excepted). `docs/agents/comment-debt-plan.md` records how the last 973 comments were relocated.
27	
28	## Commands (from the repo root)
29	
30	Node 24 (`.node-version`) and pnpm 12.18.0 are pinned.
31	
32	```sh
33	pnpm install
34	pnpm typecheck          # effect-tsrs --strict --type-check per project: Effect diagnostics fail the build
35	pnpm typecheck:tsc      # patched tsc -b, the comparison checker; not a CI step
36	pnpm typecheck:parity   # compares effect-tsrs with patched tsc, then plain tsrs with Effect codes excluded
37	pnpm typecheck:fast     # plain tsrs: fast feedback without Effect diagnostics
38	pnpm typecheck:effect   # alias of typecheck:tsc, kept for existing callers
39	pnpm bump:checkers      # bumps both checker pins, installs, reports the bundled tsrs revision, runs parity
40	pnpm check:ledger       # counts lint disables and Effect diagnostic overrides; it only shrinks
41	pnpm check:comments     # counts prose comments per package (docs/agents/comment-debt-plan.md); it only shrinks
42	pnpm lint               # oxlint --type-aware
43	pnpm format             # oxfmt; CI runs format:check
44	pnpm test               # Vitest "unit" project only
45	pnpm test:privacy       # Vitest "privacy" project only; NOT part of pnpm test
46	pnpm test:coverage      # both projects with v8 coverage, written to coverage/lcov.info (CI uploads it to Codecov)
47	pnpm test:ci            # test:coverage plus test-report.junit.xml for Codecov test analytics (CI runs this)
48	pnpm test <path>        # one file, e.g. pnpm test packages/domain/src/people/SignIn.test.ts
49	pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build
50	```
51	
52	CI runs `typecheck`, `check:ledger`, `check:comments`, `format:check`, `lint`, `test`, then the web build; the privacy suite is a separate required job. There is no root `dev` script: `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web dev` serves the UI only, and the app calls the API at `window.location.origin`. Exercise sign-in and end-to-end flows on a deployed stage.
53	
54	## Layout and boundaries
55	
56	- `packages/domain` — Effect schemas and services by concept (`people/`, `email/`); depends only on `effect`.
57	- `packages/api` — the `HttpApi` declaration shared by the Worker and the typed web client; depends on `domain`.
58	- `packages/cloudflare` — all Cloudflare adapters plus the `MainWorker` and `SubmissionWorker` entries; the only package that touches the Alchemy runtime.
59	- `apps/web` — one Vite project with two entries, the Foldkit app (`index.html`) and the plain-TypeScript answer page (`answer.html`), plus a separate build (`vite.site.config.ts`) that prerenders the landing page (`site.html`, `src/site/`) into `dist-site`.
60	- `packages/emails` — React Email templates and rendering. `packages/testing` — privacy harness. `infra` — Alchemy stack, scripts, Playwright e2e, privacy sweep. `tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat` — local lint rules.
61	
62	## Toolchain traps
63	
64	- Effect is 4.1.2, not 3.x. Import from `effect/Effect`, `effect/Schema`, `effect/http-api`, `effect/http/...`; there is no `@effect/platform` v3-style API here. Copy the import style from neighboring files.
65	- TypeScript 7 (native compiler) with `tsc -b`. A new package needs its own `tsconfig.json` and an entry in the root `tsconfig.json` references.
66	- `scripts/` is a `checkJs` project (`scripts/tsconfig.json`: `allowJs`, `checkJs`, declarations only) and part of `pnpm typecheck`, so the fence and ledger scripts are typed like the rest of the tree. Those files run in Node outside the Effect runtime, so the Effect language service turns its node-builtin and global rules off for that project only; every Effect rule that applies to Effect code stays at `error`.
67	- Stricter than defaults: `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax` (use `import type`), and relative imports carry explicit `.ts`/`.tsx` extensions.
68	- Lint bans `any` and type assertions (`as Foo`) outside `*.test.ts` (`consistent-type-assertions: never`). Decode with Effect Schema or use typed helpers instead.
69	- All user-facing text comes from `apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts` or `packages/emails/src/messages/catalog.ts`; `no-literal-ui-text` fails otherwise. HTML shells must hold no visible text and an empty `<title>` (asserted in `messages.test.ts`). Plurals use `<base>.one`/`.other`.
70	- The lint plugin enforces the boundaries: `domain`/`api` may not import `cloudflare:*`, Alchemy, or Foldkit, and `apps/web/src/answer/**` may not import React, Base UI, Foldkit, or the HttpApi client.
71	- Keep the answer entry plain TypeScript within its budget (JS ≤ 10 KB gzip critical path, CSS ≤ 2 KB inline, HTML ≤ 8 KB); no framework, per ADR 0008.
72	
73	## Tests
74	
75	- Tests are colocated `*.test.ts`. A privacy test must be named `*.privacy.test.ts` or CI never runs it.
76	- Use `@effect/vitest` (`it.effect` for Effect programs). Prefer a property or a model for a domain rule, and keep an example test for a seam. Make a new property fail on a planted bug, then remove that bug, before you trust the test.
77	- Adapter tests use `@alchemy.run/test`'s `Test.make({ dev: true })` against local workerd and are slow (deploy timeouts up to 240 s); run the single file you need.
78	- A new API endpoint must be classified in `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts` or the package will not typecheck; `registry.privacy.test.ts` checks the runtime declaration too.
79	- End-to-end tests run against a local stage by default: `pnpm test:e2e` builds the web app and starts `alchemy dev` on `infra/tests/e2e/stack.ts`, which deploys the real `MainWorker` (Durable Object, D1, sign-in and email-code handlers) to local workerd at `http://localhost:1337`. Add `E2E_BASE_URL=https://pr-<n>.app.surveybeat.app` to run the same specs against a deployed stage. Install Chromium once with `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/infra exec playwright install chromium`. The SPEC §7 flow in `flow.spec.ts` stays `test.fixme`: its answer step needs the separate `SubmissionWorker`, which the local stack does not deploy.
80	
81	## Infra
82	
83	- Every Cloudflare resource is declared in `infra/alchemy.run.ts`; no dashboard edits, no wrangler config.
84	- Run Alchemy from the repo root: the Organization DO migrations path (`packages/cloudflare/migrations`) is relative to the working directory. Build the web app first; the Main Worker serves `apps/web/dist`.
85	- `pnpm infra:deploy --stage dev-<name>` reads the sign-in allowlist at deploy time. Who may create an Organization is `infra/org-creation-allowlist.yaml`, per stage.
86	- Non-production stages never send real email; sends are recorded in D1's `captured_email`. Only `production` sends.
87	- The Submission Worker must keep every observability channel off. `pnpm check:observability --stage <stage>` reads the deployed settings back; the canary sweep proves no logs are kept. Stage scripts need `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.
88	- New SQL migrations: numbered files in `packages/cloudflare/migrations` (Durable Object) or `packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations` (D1).
89

content.content:
SessionModel,
  SessionResult,
  signInView,
} from "./session.ts";

export const Model = Schema.Struct({
  url: Url,
  route: AppRoute,
  session: SessionModel,

  browserLocale: Schema.NullOr(Locale),
  languageBusy: Schema.Boolean,
  languageFailure: Schema.Option(Failure),

  navMenu: Popover.Model,
  accountMenu: Popover.Model,

  teams: LoadedTeams,
  createTeamName: Schema.String,
  createTeamTimeZone: Schema.String,
  createTeamLeadEmail: Schema.String,
...
  size: Schema.String,
  sizeSaved: Schema.Boolean,
  sizeBusy: Schema.Boolean,
  sizeFailure: Schema.Option(Failure),
  sizeOpen: Schema.Boolean,
  aiBusy: Schema.Boolean,
  aiFailure: Schema.Option(Failure),
  defaultLanguageBusy: Schema.Boolean,
  defaultLanguageFailure: Schema.Option(Failure),
  peopleBusy: Schema.Boolean,
  peopleFailure: Schema.Option(Failure),
  failedEmails: LoadedFailedEmails,

...
  SignInCodeSent: { sent: Schema.Boolean },
  SignInCodeChecked: { verified: Schema.Boolean },
  CreateOrgNameChanged: { name: Schema.String },
  SubmitCreateOrg: {},
  ChooseOrgClicked: { organizationId: OrganizationId },
  LanguageChanged: { value: Schema.String },
  UpdatedOwnLanguage: { chosen: Schema.Boolean, outcome: OutcomeVoid },

  GotNavMenuMessage: { message: Popover.Message },
  GotAccountMenuMessage: { message: Popover.Message },

...
  SubmitSize: {},
  UpdatedSettings: { outcome: OutcomeVoid },
  AiProcessingToggled: { isOn: Schema.Boolean },
  UpdatedAiProcessing: { outcome: OutcomeVoid },
  DefaultLanguageChanged: { value: Schema.String },
  UpdatedDefaultLanguage: { outcome: OutcomeVoid },
  GotFailedEmails: { outcome: OutcomeFailedEmails },
  ResendFailedEmailClicked: { sendId: SendId },
  ResentFailedEmail: { sendId: SendId, outcome: OutcomeFailedEmailStatus },
  PolledFailedEmail: { sendId: SendId, outcome: OutcomeFailedEmailStatus },
  GrantAdminClicked: { personId: PersonId },
...
  args: { organizationId: OrganizationId },
  messages: [Message.GotSession],
  execute: ({ organizationId }) =>
    runSessionCall((api) => api.auth.chooseOrganization({ payload: { organizationId } })).pipe(
      Effect.map((result) => Message.GotSession({ result })),
    ),
});

export const UpdateOwnLanguage = Command.define("UpdateOwnLanguage", {
  args: {
    locale: Schema.optionalKey(Schema.NullOr(Locale)),
    detectedLocale: Schema.optionalKey(Locale),
  },
  messages: [Message.UpdatedOwnLanguage],
  execute: (args) => {
    const chosen = args.locale !== undefined;
    return runApi(
      (api) => api.directory.updateOwnLanguage({ payload: args }),
      () => Message.UpdatedOwnLanguage({ chosen, outcome: { _tag: "Success" } }),
      (failure) => Message.UpdatedOwnLanguage({ chosen, outcome: { _tag: "Failure", failure } }),
    );
  },
});

export const ListTeams = Command.define("ListTeams", {
  messages: [Message.GotTeams],
...
  execute: ({ aiProcessing }) =>

# German ships as typed catalogs per locale, a prerendered answer page per locale, and a bilingual Template

Release 2 adds German to the app, the answer page, and emails ([research](../research/german-localization.md)).

- **Catalogs:** each catalog gets a `de.ts` beside the English one, typed so a missing key, an extra key, or a wrong `{placeholder}` fails typecheck. The message functions take the locale instead of the fixed `"en"`; plurals, dates, and numbers come from `Intl` for that locale.
- **Which language:** a Person's own setting, then the browser's languages, then the Organization's default. Emails render in the language stored with the send when it is created.
- **Answer page:** one prerendered page per locale (`/a`, `/de/a`), each loading only its own answer catalog. The Invitation link picks the page from the recipient's language. ADR 0008's budget applies to each page separately.
- **Words:** informal "du". Pulse and Team stay English; Round → Runde, Lead → Teamleitung, Organization → Organisation, Submission → Einsendung. Claude drafts, the product owner reviews in the PR.
- **Template:** the weekly team health Template ships in both languages; a new Pulse copies its Questions in the Lead's language. Existing Pulses keep their Questions.
- **Privacy:** the language is never stored with a Submission or an Answer. In a small Team it could single out the one German reader.

## Consequences

- The budget test runs per answer page.
- Pages rendered in `MainWorker.ts` (delivery time, unsubscribe) hold hard-coded English and must move to the catalog.
- Redaction gains German phone number cases.
- A Team with mixed languages sees the Pulse's Questions in the language they were created in.
----

The `apps/web` build runs `vite.site.config.ts` after the app build (`vite.config.ts`), so both outputs come from one package.

# English is the only shipped language for now; German stays a path back

English is the only language the app, the answer page, the landing page, and emails ship in. This supersedes the Release 2 German rollout of [ADR 0018](0018-german-localization.md) for now, and the German landing page in [ADR 0020](0020-landing-page-is-a-static-site-worker.md).

- **Shipped language:** `Locale` is `Schema.Literals(["en"])`. The `Locale` type, `messagesFor(locale)`, the `Record<Locale, …>` tables, and the API fields `locale`, `detectedLocale`, and `defaultLocale` stay, so a language comes back by adding its literal.
- **Removed:** the German catalogs, the German answer page (`/de/a`), the German landing page (`/de/`), the German weekly team health Template, the account menu's language field, and the Settings "Default language" section.
- **Kept:** the typed-catalog approach, so a missing key, an extra key, or a wrong `{placeholder}` still fails typecheck. Redaction's German phone-number cases stay.
- **Stored values:** rows that already hold `de` read back as unset (`person.locale`, `person.detected_locale`) or as English (`organization.default_locale`, the locale of a stored email). No migration rewrites them.
- **Bringing German back:** add the literal to `Locale`, a catalog per surface (web, answer, emails), the bilingual weekly team health Template, an answer page per locale with its own budget check, and the language picker. The stored values then read as German again without a migration.

## Consequences

- Every page and email renders in English. A `lang=de` or `/de/` link falls back to English.
- A Person who had chose German no longer sees the German UI, and cannot change the language in the app. The API still accepts a language, so a later client can set one.
- Adding a language is a code change in the catalogs and the Template, not a data migration.

content.text:
German is removed from the English-only worktree and the locale plumbing is kept. Everything is uncommitted in `/home/ubuntu/english-only`, and all eight validation commands pass on the final tree.

## Changes

**Locale core (`packages/domain`)**
- `people/Locale.ts`: `Locale = Schema.Literals(["en"])`. `matchLocale`, `browserLocale`, `resolveLocale` are unchanged. I added `localeOrNull` and `localeOr`, lenient readers that map anything that isn't a known locale to unset or the fallback.
- `email/Email.ts`: `EmailLocale` gets a `Schema.catchDecoding` so a stored `de` decodes as `en` instead of failing. This covers queued sends in `SqlSendRepository`.
- `pulses/Template.ts`: the German branch is removed. The record is still keyed by `Locale`, and `weeklyTeamHealth(locale)` keeps its signature.

**Cloudflare**
- `SqlDirectory.ts`: `person.locale`, `person.detected_locale` and `organization.default_locale` are read as plain strings and mapped leniently. No migration.
- `organization/Directory.ts`: uses the shared helpers instead of its own copies.

**Web app**
- Deleted `messages/de.ts`, `messages/answer.de.ts`, `answer/de.ts`, `de/answer.html`.
- `messages/locale.ts`: the `tables` map is English only.
- `catalog.ts`: removed `language.*`, `settings.defaultLanguage*`, `site.footer.language`.
- `app/directory.ts` and `app/App.ts`: removed the account-menu language field, the Settings "Default language" section, their messages, update branches and commands, and the `shellView` language argument.
- `site/render.ts`: removed the language link, `/de` path, and `pathFor`. `og:locale` is a table.
- `vite.config.ts`, `vite.site.config.ts`: removed the `/de` pages and the answer-de entry.

**Emails (`packages/emails`)**
- Deleted `messages/de.ts`. `messages/index.ts` has an English-only table.
- `links.ts`: `answerPath` and `langQuery` are table-driven, English only.

**Infra**
- `lighthouse-gate.ts`: no German page.
- `answer.spec.ts`: removed the German test.

**Docs**
- New `docs/adr/0025-english-only-for-now.md`.
- Supersession line at the top of ADR 0018.
- SPEC lines 135 and 252 updated.

**Tests**
- Deleted or rewritten the German cases in the domain, Cloudflare, email, and web suites. The English coverage they carried is kept.
- `SqlDirectory.test.ts`: new test that a row holding `de` reads back as unset.
- `EmailTemplates.test.ts`: a stored `de` email decodes as English.
- `DirectoryApi.test.ts`: `de` is now refused with 400.
- Pruned 12 obsolete German email snapshots. The snapshot diff is deletions only.

## Decisions that differ from the brief

- **Sign-in language sync removed.** `App.ts` used to send `UpdateOwnLanguage({ detectedLocale })` at sign-in. That is a language sent from the UI, so I removed it. The domain command, the API endpoint, and `PersonLanguageSet` are kept.
- **ADR 0020 also marked superseded.** It prescribes the German `/de/` landing page. AGENTS.md says a contradicting change must be recorded, so I added the same one-line note. You did not ask for this.
- **`answerPath` and `langQuery` kept as tables.** They are not deleted, so `lang` plumbing stays for a later second locale.
- **Some tests lost their meaning.** Locale precedence (person, then browser, then organization) can no longer be tested with two values. Those tests now assert English. The precedence coverage returns when a second locale does.
- **Two lines of cover moved.** The placeholder check in the web and email catalogs now mutates the English table. The `budget.test.ts` cross-check against the other locale's save label is gone.

- `pnpm test:privacy`: exit 0, 9 files passed, 241 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build`: exit 0. The app and landing page are English only. The budget test passes on the English answer page (HTML 7.70 KB raw, 5.60 KB gzip critical JS).

## Notes

- **Dependencies were not installed.** The brief said they were, but `node_modules` was missing. I ran `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`. I skipped the `prepare` script because it runs `git config --local core.hooksPath`, a git write. As a result, `core.hooksPath` is not set in this worktree and the fence hooks are inactive.
